forms: say the sound of the letter
say the word after the teacher
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child says each letter-sound short and clean (/b/ not buh, /m/ not muh), keeps l and r and short and long vowels apart, and says words without adding a vowel at the end. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.G.mastery: The child uses Good morning, Good afternoon and Good evening at the right time, answers How are you? with I am fine, thank you, and greets elders politely. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which child is sitting well to read
what is wrong in the picture
ENGL.G1.READIN.T1_PRE_READING.READING_PO.mastery: The child picks out a good reading posture (back straight, feet on the floor, book on the desk at a comfortable distance, good light) and the book the right way up. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the sounds, then the word
ENGL.G1.READIN.T1_PRE_READING.DECODE_WOR.mastery: The child says the sound of each letter left to right and blends them into a word (c-a-t, cat; s-i-t, sit), reading three- and four-letter words with the letters learnt. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T1_VERB_TO_BE_PRESENT_T.V.mastery: The child picks am, is and are in sentences and uses them to introduce self and others: I am Amina. She is my friend. You are my teacher. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which child is ready to write
how do we hold the pencil
what is wrong in the picture
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T1_PRE_WRITING.WRITING_PO.mastery: The child picks out a good writing posture: sitting up, feet on the floor, the book straight in front, the other hand holding the page, the pencil held between thumb and first two fingers. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T1_PRE_WRITING.PRE_WRITIN.mastery: The child traces and copies lines, curves, circles and zigzags from left to right with a light, steady hand, keeping within the lines. Evidence rule: the teacher sees it in two pieces of the learner's own work, scored with the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /iː/, /ɪ/, /aɪ/, /dʒ/, /k/, /l/, /m/, /n/, /ɒ/, /ɔː/ and /p/ in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example sheep, sit, kite, jug, kettle, leg, mat, nest, pot, ball, pen). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say a sentence about the picture
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child says a short sentence of three or more words with a theme word (This is my school. I have a pencil.), not one word. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: match the capital to the small letter
ENGL.G1.READIN.T2_PRE_READING.CAPITAL_SM.mastery: The child picks out capital and small letters in a text and matches each pair, including those that look different (A and a, B and b, G and g). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T2_VERBS_TO_DO_PRESENT_.S.mastery: The child picks out I, he, she and it in an oral text and uses them as the subject: he for a boy or man, she for a girl or woman, it for a thing or animal, without repeating the subject. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T2_VERBS_TO_DO_PRESENT_.D.mastery: The child picks out do and does in an oral text and uses does with he, she and it and do with I and you, with a plain verb after: She does her homework. Do you like milk? Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with this letter
match the letter to the picture
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.L.mastery: The child links q, r, s, t, u, v, w, x, y and z to their sounds (q for queen, v for van, x for box, y for yam) and tells the sound from the letter name. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.F.mastery: The child carries out a one-step spoken instruction (Stand up. Bring the cup. Put the book under the chair.) by doing it or answering. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: point to the letter I say
ENGL.G1.READIN.T3_PRE_READING.LETTER_NAM.mastery: The child names letters clearly when shown them in any order (q, r, s, t, u, v, w, x, y, z), without singing from a. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T3_VERB_TO_HAVE_PRESENT.H.mastery: The child picks out have and has and uses has with he, she and it and have with I and you: I have a sister. He has a ball. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T3_VERB_TO_HAVE_PRESENT.O.mastery: The child picks out me, him, her and it in a text and uses them after a verb or a small word like to: Give me the book. I love her. Mama called him. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T3_HANDWRITING.FORMED_LET.mastery: The child picks out the correctly formed letter (closed a, s the right way round, tall letters tall) from poorly formed ones in a text. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: write the letters on the line
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T3_HANDWRITING.FORM_LETTE.mastery: The child forms each small letter from the right starting point (round letters from the top, like c), the right size and the right way round, writes capital letters correctly, and writes words left to right. Evidence rule: the teacher sees it in two pieces of the learner's own work, scored with the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: circle the letter in the word
ENGL.G1.READIN.T4_PRE_READING.LETTER_IN_.mastery: The child finds a given letter at the start, middle or end of a word, small or capital (m in mat, Amina, ham). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: make a word with these letters
ENGL.G1.READIN.T4_PRE_READING.BUILD_WORD.mastery: The child puts letter cards in order to make a short word (m-a-t, t-e-a-m) and finds a missing letter. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T4_SINGULAR_AND_PLURALS.P.mastery: The child adds -s to make most plurals (cup, cups) and -es after s, x, ch and sh (bus, buses; box, boxes; dish, dishes), and keeps the -s after a number (two cups). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /s/, /l/, /ɪ/ and /p/ in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example sun, leg, pin, pot). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T5_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.N.mastery: The child looks at the person speaking, uses a face that fits what is said (a smile for thank you, a sorry face for sorry) and simple gestures (a nod for yes, a wave for goodbye), as is polite at home and school. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: match the letter to the sound
ENGL.G1.READIN.T5_PRE_READING.MATCH_LETT.mastery: The child matches the letters S, L, I and P (and others learnt) to the sounds they make and picks the letter for a sound heard. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T5_TENSE_PRESENT_SIMPLE.P.mastery: The child picks out present simple verbs and uses them for what is done every day, with -s after he, she and it: I wake up at six. She washes her face. We go to school. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /f/, /n/, /h/, /ɒ/ (pot) and /ɔː/ (ball) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example fan, nose, hat, dog, door). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T6_1_TENSE_PRESENT_CONT.P.mastery: The child names activities going on now in and out of school and uses am, is or are with -ing: I am writing. The children are playing. It is raining. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T6_SPELLING.SPELL_CVC.mastery: The child spells three- to five-letter words with the letters learnt (fan, hen, nut, bag, rug, cow, desk) by writing a letter for each sound in order. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T7_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /b/, /r/, /ʌ/ (u) and /g/ in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example bed, rat, cup, goat). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.READIN.T7_WORD_READING.SIGHT_WOR.mastery: The child reads common sight words at a glance (the, is, was, said, are, you, my, of), and does not sound them out letter by letter. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T7_TENSE_SIMPLE_PAST_TE.P.mastery: The child picks out words ending in -ed and -d in a text and uses them for things that happened: Yesterday I washed my hands. We played football. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T7_SPELLING.B_D_LETTERS.mastery: The child writes and picks b, d, p, q, u and n the right way round and up (bag, dog, pen, queen, up, net). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /k/, /d/ and /w/ in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example cat, kite, doll, window). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match the word to the picture
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.T.mastery: The child chooses the theme word that fits a picture or sentence (for example eyes, ears, friend, road, chief, share, phone, two, tap) and does not swap it for a word of the same group. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.READIN.T8_FLUENCY.READ_ALOUD.mastery: The child reads a few short sentences aloud, blending new words and reading sight words at a glance, with few long stops, pointing under the words. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

forms: read it happily, read it sadly
ENGL.G1.READIN.T8_FLUENCY.READ_WITH_FEEL.mastery: The child lets the voice show a feeling in the text (happy, sad, surprised), lifts the voice for a question and stops at full stops. Evidence rule: the teacher hears it done right on two different days, scored with the observation rubric (PLAN_OBSERVATION_RUBRICS.md); a tapped answer cannot show it.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T8_DEMONSTRATIVES_THIS_.D.mastery: The child picks out this, that, these and those and uses this and these for things near, that and those for things far, with one or many: This is my nose. Those are your shoes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T9_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: The child hears the sounds /k/, /j/ (y as in yes), /l/ and /s/ in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example cup, yes, lamp, sit). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word names a person, thing or place
ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T9_NOUNS_COMMON_AND_PRO.N.mastery: The child picks out naming words for people, things and places, tells a general name (girl, town) from a special name (Wanjiru, Nakuru), and uses both in short sentences. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T9_PUNCTUATION_CAPITAL_.C.mastery: The child picks out capital letters, small letters and full stops in a text, starts every sentence with a capital and ends it with a full stop. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T10_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /æ/ (cat), /ɔː/ (chalk), /iː/ (chief), /uː/ (school), /ɔɪ/ (boy) and /eɪ/ (day) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example cat, door, tree, food, toy, play). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T10_SIMPLE_PREPOSITIONS_..mastery: The child picks out the position words in a text and uses them in short sentences about safety: The knife is in the drawer. Stand behind the line. Play outside. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which mark goes at the end
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T10_PUNCTUATION_CAPITAL_..mastery: The child picks out question marks and capitals in a text and writes a question that starts with a capital and ends with a question mark. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T11_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /ʃ/ (sh), /tʃ/ (ch) and the two th sounds /θ/ (thin) and /ð/ (this) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example share, chair, thank, this). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.READIN.T11_COMPREHENSION.PREDICT.mastery: The child looks at the title and pictures and says what the story will be about or what will happen next, and why. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.READIN.T11_COMPREHENSION.ANSWER_.mastery: The child answers who, what and where questions from a short text or picture story, and simple how did he feel questions from clues (he cried: sad). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T11_ADJECTIVES_ONE_AND_T..mastery: The child names describing words (big, small, tall, kind, clean, red) and uses them before the noun to talk about people, places and things: a tall chief, a clean market. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T11_GUIDED_WRITING.PICTUR.mastery: The child says what a picture shows and what is happening in it (The chief is talking to the people), not just one object in it. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: write a sentence with the word
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T11_GUIDED_WRITING.WRITE_.mastery: The child writes a simple sentence of his or her own with four- to six-letter words, a capital letter, spaces between words and a full stop. Evidence rule: two pieces of the learner's own writing marked Meeting Expectations or above on the KICD rubric indicator.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T12_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /e/ (bed), /iː/ (see) and /eə/ (chair, share) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example bed, sleep, chair). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T12_POSSESSIVES_MY_OUR_H..mastery: The child picks out possessives in a text and uses them to show who owns something: my bag, our school, her pen, his cup, their house, its tail. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: choose the word for the gap
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T12_GUIDED_WRITING.FILL_G.mastery: The child chooses the word that fits the gap in meaning and form (We live ___ together: in peace) by reading the whole sentence. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /ʊ/ (book, put) and /eɪ/ (play, game) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example book, foot, play, take). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.READIN.T13_COMPREHENSION.WORD_FR.mastery: The child uses the picture and the words around a new word to say what it means. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T13_YES_NO_QUESTIONS_WIT..mastery: The child picks out yes or no questions with can, may and will and answers in full: Can you use a phone? Yes, I can. May I go out? Yes, you may. Will it rain? No, it will not. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T13_GUIDED_WRITING.WORD_O.mastery: The child rearranges three to five jumbled words into a sentence that makes sense, starting with the word with a capital letter. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T14_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /dʒ/ (jug, orange), /s/ and /ŋ/ (sing, ring) in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example jump, six, string). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T14_ADVERBS_OF_PLACE.ADVE.mastery: The child picks out adverbs of place in sentences and uses them to say where things and people are: Come here. The goats are outside. The shop is far. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: which word starts with the sound
point to the picture with the sound
ENGL.G1.LISTEN.T15_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO..mastery: The child hears the sounds /l/, /s/ and /r/, telling l from r in spoken words and picks out the words that have them (for example light, sun, rain). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

ENGL.G1.LANGUA.T15_INTERJECTIONS_OF_SUR..mastery: The child picks out words of surprise (Oh! Wow! What!) in a text and uses them in short sentences with an exclamation mark. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: write a sentence with a describing word
ENGL.G1.WRITIN.T15_GUIDED_WRITING.DESCRI.mastery: The child writes a short sentence that uses a describing word before the noun (The tap has clean water. I have a green tree.). Evidence rule: two pieces of the learner's own writing marked Meeting Expectations or above on the KICD rubric indicator.
